scope: Recorded GCC enabled options and LLVM observed Running-pass names, O0-O2, x86-64 baseline only; every distinct item assigned once. Not proof of successful transforms or exhaustive optimization coverage.
limitations: Recorded report predates combined code revision; assembly metrics must not be relabeled as combined-code measurements.
GCC configured_passes_on and LLVM analysis listings are not claimed mapped; requested ledger maps enabled_options and observed_passes only.
GCC boolean options only: parameter-valued policies, target tuning defaults and unobserved passes are not an exhaustive compiler specification.
LLVM pass names are deduplicated, losing invocation counts/order; backend machine passes are not fully inventoried by this trace.
O3, other CPU targets, native ISA, LTO, PGO, C++, OpenMP and coroutines are outside this inventory.
Code evidence is source inspection, not new positive runtime/codegen/performance tests. Status applies to the whole family, never certifies every listed pass.

integer-simplification.remaining: Existing typed identities, signed/unsigned powers of two and limited u32 reciprocals do not establish InstCombine parity. Next: bounded small-multiply/bit-test rules and shared quotient+remainder recipes; signed/u64 reciprocal rules need separate target cost evidence. Float2Int transformations remain unverified, not covered by integer folding.

value-propagation-and-redundancy.remaining: Local exact-cell/copy facts and selected AST facts exist; no shared global CSE/GVN/PRE or SCCP engine was identified. Add fixed-size block-local pure-value cache first. Later CFG predecessors/dominators and versioned facts permit global propagation; SSA is a candidate representation, not a prerequisite for the local stage.

dead-work-and-memory.remaining: Straight-line exact frame-cell forwarding/overwritten stores and target dead results exist. Heap/global alias-aware DSE, bit-level DCE, allocation elimination, load/store motion and loop load elimination remain missing/unverified. First remove provably unused pure local initializers with existing escape/effect facts; preserve volatile/atomic/trapping access contracts.

control-and-switch.remaining: Constant pure decisions and balanced switch dispatch exist, wasm keeps dense br_table. Value tables, bit-test clusters, compare merging, general jump threading/diamond conversion and tail merging are not established. Extend shared switch strategy with bounded tables/bitsets first; cross-block rewrites need explicit CFG and all external label entries.

scalar-replacement-and-promotion.remaining: Selected scalar homes/wasm locals and cell forwarding are not general SROA/mem2reg. Next: nonescaping aggregate fields with stable identities and bounded scalarization, then join-aware promotion. Shared SSA becomes useful for many merge values, not required to select locals or split a straight-line object.

loop-motion-and-induction.remaining: Loop lowering and loop-weighted local selection exist; no general shared loop discovery, induction rewrite or LICM identified. Build bounded CFG/dominators/natural-loop facts, then hoist pure nontrapping invariant expressions with effect and zero-trip proofs. SSA/LCSSA is useful for sophisticated loop rewriting, not logically required for first safe hoists.

loop-shape-and-unrolling.remaining: Direct loop lowering is not rotation/deletion/unrolling/unswitching. Add only after loop trip/effect/entry proofs and code-growth budgets; start exact small constant trip counts. Distribution and unswitching need dependence and profitability evidence. No blanket SSA requirement for syntax-local constant loops.

vectorization.remaining: Arm64 has selected integer NEON operations plus lane fallback; x86/wasm GNU-vector lowering is lane-wise in inspected paths. Explicit packed SSE2/wasm simd128 lowering is a distinct cheap target task before automatic vectorization. General loop/SLP vectorization needs dependence, alignment, reductions, legality, tail handling and target cost models; SSA alone does not provide these.

inlining-and-calls.remaining: Native inlining exists with different target eligibility; wasm has no equivalent inliner in inspected path. No general sibling-call lowering identified. Share bounded eligibility/cost policy first, then implement wasm parameter/result/scope remapping and restricted tail ABI hooks. Partial inlining, indirect promotion and general varargs optimization remain separate work; none requires generic SSA merely to inline AST bodies.

interprocedural-and-global.remaining: Prepass function facts and TU emission filtering are limited evidence, not whole-program IPA. Require explicit call graph, linkage/interposition/escape summaries before pure-const propagation, argument elimination, specialization or merging. Linker section GC is not compiler global DCE or identical-code folding. C++ devirtualization is outside this C compiler scope; C indirect calls still matter.

library-and-idiom.remaining: Constant __builtin_strcmp proof and selected explicit memory builtins exist; plain-libcall, strlen/printf value folding, CRC idioms, memcpy-chain optimization and loop idiom recognition are not established. Share bounded literal/known-size recipes with freestanding/builtin controls, object bounds and overlap semantics; do not infer library purity merely from a spelling.

machine-register-allocation.remaining: Native uses persistent homes plus temporary allocation, not general IRA/LRA/live-range splitting. Extend scoped liveness/rematerialization only after measured pressure/spill cases; shared facts, target register/ABI policy. Wasm locals are unbounded VM locations, so physical register algorithms do not map one-for-one.

machine-combining-and-addressing.remaining: Instruction selection and limited extension/copy cleanup exist; no full GCC machine-combine equivalent established. Next cheap work: typed indexed addresses, immediate stores, compare/flags reuse with exact effects and profitable small constant multiplication; a64/x64 encodings and wasm address-stack costs remain target-owned.

machine-layout-and-scheduling.remaining: Emission order/alignment are not evidence of profile-guided block placement or dependency scheduling. First audit target-specific defaults and static likely/unlikely placement; measure code size/fetch effects. Later bounded native instruction scheduling requires dependency/latency data. Wasm structured branches/engine scheduling need a different profitability model.

abi-frame-security-and-debug.remaining: x86 has conservative proven-frame-free leaf omission; ABI/frame/debug mechanisms differ by target. General shrink wrapping, stack-adjust combining, security/instrumentation options and debug assignment tracking are separate policies/correctness features, not all required speed transforms. Inventory GCC defaults do not prove probe emission or vcc option support; audit driver and target contracts individually.

fp-semantics-policy.remaining: These mostly constrain legal transformations and observable FP behavior; enabled does not mean fast-math. Verify option handling/rounding/errno/exceptions separately. Existing integer identities do not authorize FP reassociation, x*0, reciprocal approximation or vectorization under relaxed semantics.

alias-alignment-and-assumptions.remaining: Object/escape/overlap facts serve exact frame cells; no general TBAA/points-to/global alias analysis identified. Add bounded disjoint object and immutable-value facts before moving memory; strict-aliasing language policy and alignment assumptions require explicit front-end contracts and adversarial union/char/overlap tests. Analysis invalidation itself is infrastructure.

pipeline-and-metadata.remaining: Pass-manager wrappers, lowering of LLVM intrinsics, remarks and metadata maintenance do not each require a vcc optimization pass. Separate user-visible semantics from representation plumbing. Allocation tokens/memory profile metadata need investigation before claiming any relevant source-level capability.

other-language-lowering.remaining: Coroutine/OpenMP pass names appearing on this C probe do not demonstrate transformations or define supported source languages. Track coroutine/OpenMP support separately from the C O2 optimization backlog.

atomic-and-unreachable-lowering.remaining: Atomic target lowering exists; inline versus libcall selection, ordering, target feature fallback and unreachable trap policy need explicit driver/codegen contracts. These are relevant C capabilities, not automatically delivered by optimizer passes.

inventory_extraction.llvm: clang FLAGS -S probe.c -Xclang -fdebug-pass-manager: deduplicated ^Running pass: (\S+) on
